# Nexus Code v1.1.1

**Maturity:** Stable release for Nexus Code v1.1.1.

This release delivers the complete Nexus Code multi-agent orchestration architecture, serialized git integration with verified execution receipts, typed inter-agent communication, operation replay, and closed edge cases for cancellation idempotency, message du
- Multi-agent orchestration with deterministic parallel work units and per-resource slot reservations.
- Serialized Git integration queue with candidate digests and verified execution receipts.
- Typed inter-agent communication channels (`request`, `observation`, `artifact`, `verdict`).
- Operation timeline replay with schema version 2 persistence and safe legacy migration.
- Cancellation idempotency and late result suppression.
- Durability-positive message acknowledgment and structured retry classification.
- Proven prompt submission provenance (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`) protecting message injection against model outputs, tool outputs, and non-Nexus user notes.
- Protected task envelope replay failure propagation across single- and multi-record queries.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.0.0: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js; Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Highlights

### Deterministic parallel work units

An operation may now run more than one work unit at a time:

```json
{
  "objective": "Add a --dry-run flag",
  "policy": { "maxConcurrentUnits": 2 },
  "resources": [
    { "id": "primary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m1" },
    { "id": "secondary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m2", "maxConcurrentUnits": 1 }
  ],
  "units": [
    { "id": "impl", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "docs", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "test", "role": "tester", "dependsOn": ["impl"], "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "review", "role": "reviewer", "dependsOn": ["impl", "test"], "requires": { "independentOf": ["impl"] } }
  ]
}
```

- The scheduler returns an ordered due-set: required units first, then the longest unfinished dependent chain, then the operation's declared unit order. The same persisted state always produces the same due-set.
- Concurrency defaults to **1**. An operation that does not opt in behaves as it did in v1.0.0: one unit in flight.
- Per-resource slots are reserved for the duration of a run, so two units pinned to one single-slot resource serialise. A unit whose qualified slots are busy stays `RUNNABLE` — it is not parked and not escalated.
- One unit's failure does not touch a batch-mate. Cancelling aborts every in-flight unit and leaves each resumable. A restart reconciles every unit that was in flight.

### Retained worktrees are named

A unit worktree with uncommitted or ignored files is kept rather than destroyed, and the event log now says which worktree was kept and why (`WORKTREE_RETAINED`). A clean lifecycle still leaves no unit worktree behind.

### Serialised git integration with evidenced receipts

Concurrent isolated units complete at unpredictable times, but they share one integration worktree. Integration is now a queue: one merge at a time, in completion order, with `INTEGRATION_QUEUED` and `INTEGRATION_SKIPPED` events. Each receipt records:

- the unit's branch and commit, and the resulting `integratedCommit`;
- the **candidate digest** of the tree that was merged (omitted, never fabricated, when the worktree was already gone);
- the **executed verifier** the unit was accepted with (omitted when it produced none);
- a 1-based **sequence** so a reviewer can reconstruct merge order.

The focused tests pass, but I found one functional regression on the vLLM path and two real gaps in the other areas you asked about. I worked in detached worktrees (`~/nexus-wt/rv-wp1107` at 5fde750a, plus a temporary baseline at 3eea888a) with a throwaway HOME. I removed both worktrees at the end. ## Findings, by severity

**HIGH: vLLM strict mode makes `write_file` and `run_command` fail at execution.**
- `cli/src/core/tool_grammar_provider.ts:35-41` turns every optional parameter into a required, nullable one. A strict-mode model will therefore emit `"overwrite": null`, `"background": null` and similar.
- The Rust core rejects those nulls. `core/src/file_ops.rs` declares `overwrite: bool`, and `core/src/runner.rs` declares `timeout_secs: u64`, `shell: String` and `background: bool`.
- I built the core from this commit and called `RustCoreBridge.executeTool` directly:
  - `write_file {overwrite:null}` returns `Invalid write_file arguments: invalid type: null, expected a boolean`.
  - `run_command` with `background:null` returns `Invalid run_command arguments: invalid type: null, expected a boolean`, and all-null fails the same way.
  - `timeout_secs`, `shell`, `cwd` and `service_name` as null each succeed on their own, as do `read_file` and `edit_file` nulls.
- Nothing in `client.ts` (around 1526 and 1792), `agent.ts` (`dispatchToolCallImpl`, around 4850) or the `executeTool` pipeline strips nulls before dispatch. I traced the agent path by reading it, not by running a full agent loop against a mock vLLM.
- The matrix would not catch this. It classifies a call as `native_valid` when it satisfies the adapted schema, and that schema allows null (`validateToolArguments` and its test at `tool_grammar_matrix.test.mjs:130`). A vLLM lane could score 100% while every `write_file` and `run_command` call fails when executed.
- The fix is to strip nulls for fields that were optional before the adapter ran. Do it in the client or the dispatch path, or make the core accept null.

**MEDIUM: REQ-PRV-109 holds only on the success path.**
- `routingHeaders()` (`client.ts:809-821`) suppresses X-Task-Class only when the cached kind is known. The commit now demotes the kind to `unknown` whenever a handshake fails, so the header is sent to a standalone server.

- It checks a `.provenance.json` inside the caller-supplied `installRoot` (`eval/tool_grammar_matrix.mjs:259-270`). That file is self-attested JSON. Nothing ties it to the files under `lib/cli/dist`, the archive contents, or `MANIFEST.sha256`. `install.sh` checks the manifest at install time, but the runner never does.
- I demonstrated three bypasses against a copy of the runner:
  - A forged `.provenance.json`, a hand-written `lib/cli/dist` and an unrelated "archive" file were accepted: `passed: true`, with the archive's SHA recorded.
  - A symlinked `lib` pointing outside `installRoot` ran the outside runtime. `path.resolve` is used and there is no `realpath`.

Codex's claim holds so far. The run is still in progress, though, and it is testing uncommitted code, not a commit.

**What's running**
- **The run:** a full `make test` that codex-root calls "CI-layout". It runs from a new Git-backed worktree, `v112-wp1107-final-git-20261104`. It has been going about 32 minutes and holds SUITE.
- **What is under test:** `7f915894` plus 12 modified files and 1 new test file. These are uncommitted fixes in that worktree. They match the findings from my reviews:
  - `agent.ts`, `client.ts` and `provider_capabilities.ts`
  - the matrix runner `eval/tool_grammar_matrix.mjs`
  - new tests, including `vllm_nullable_dispatch.test.ts` and 124 added lines in `task_class.test.ts`
- **So codex-root did pick up the review.** There is still no commit, no push, and no claims-log note saying so.

**The durable-history claim**
- **Earlier run:** the 07:35 run (`wp1107-final-git-make-test.log`) failed at least 62 top-level cases. A tool session expired at `step_loop.test.ts`. Its log names several durable-history failures.
- **Current run so far:** 731 passed and 0 failed so far (excluding the expected noise from inference-error output). The six earlier durable-history cases I checked, which cover restart during waiting, a durable operation over the workload, death after archive, and two compaction recovery cases, now pass. Two earlier failures, "AC3a: run --resume --step resumes durable state" and "AC3b: /step resumes saved objective after REPL restart", haven't been reached yet.
- **What the earlier failures were:** codex-root's own notes say they came from an invalid setup, not source defects. An archive snapshot had no `.git`, and the core directory was in the wrong place. I can only confirm the setup fix is consistent with the passing results. I haven't proven it was the cause.

**Caveats**
- **Nothing binds the result to a commit yet.** The fixes need committing, and the gate then has to run on that exact commit. Otherwise it says nothing about a head.
- **Clock skew in the log.** codex-root's heartbeats are labelled UTC but run about 2 hours 45 minutes ahead of real UTC (real time is 08:18, its heartbeat says 11:02). I'll go by file times and running processes for the silence rule, not its timestamps.
- **Not re-reviewed.** I haven't looked at the uncommitted fixes, only their file names. The independent re-review waits for the commit.

  - No `node_modules` on either side now gives `infrastructureFailure` and `passed:false`.

  - With `node_modules` present, the candidate's syntax error appears as a new TS1109 diagnostic.
- Unit cases: identical "Cannot find module" lines on both sides fail, and so do identical `bwrap:` setup failures.
- The gate is a hard-coded `error TS\d+:` regex, not the "task-supplied diagnostic regex" you described. Checkers that do not print TS codes (eslint, mypy, `cargo check`) always fail when the baseline already has errors. That fails closed but is undocumented. `eval/evaluators/code/README.md` and `SPEC-EVALUATION` still say `cargo check` is supported and still describe the old rule.
- Residual gap: identical recognised config errors on both sides, such as TS5057 (no tsconfig found), still pass vacuously. Low severity.
- 05913af5 changes the regex to `\berror(?:\s+TS\d+|\[E\d+\])?:` with the `/i` flag. The code group is now optional, so any line containing `error:` counts as recognised. That includes Node's `Error: Cannot find module '...'` and probably many sandbox errors.
- If so, F1 scenario 1 (no `node_modules`, identical lines on both sides) goes back to `passed:true`. This is from reading the diff, **not verified (host reserved)**. The fix is to require a Rust code (`error\[E\d+\]:`) or a TS code, not an optional one. The new test should include "Error: Cannot find module" on both sides.

**F2 (candidate-modified build config): PARTIAL.**

The edited config is ignored silently, though, and that is not documented. Candidate config changes are neither reported nor failed.

**F3 (syntax_ast default list): FIXED, with one pre-existing exception.**

- An explicit `files` list that includes a deleted path still fails with ENOENT, which is the old behaviour.

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Nexus Code v1.1.2** targets the full WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0. The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files; v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2.

## Release scope and status

The intended scope is the complete [WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap](../v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md), together with any already-approved corrective changes needed for the candidate. The operation message-delivery correction described below remains relevant context for the v1.1.1 predecessor.

This document records the target scope; it does not claim that the roadmap is implemented or qualified. As of this note, roadmap implementation and v1.1.2 qualification remain incomplete; completion requires recording the applicable evidence. Work-package completion, exact-head test and type gates, independent review, release-candidate qualification, and publication are still required before v1.1.2 can be called released. Track implementation and evidence in the work-package plans and release qualification record.

## Fixed

### A crash-resumed unit no longer receives a multi-message prompt's later messages twice

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

- Impact in v1.1.1: the duplicated message was advisory context only. No message was lost, and no `TurnResult`, verification, or acceptance outcome was affected.
- Regression coverage: the post-prompt crash test in `cli/test/operation_release_review.test.ts` now carries two messages. It asserts that each message appears once in the durable history and is acknowledged once.

## Correction to the v1.1.1 notes

The v1.1.1 notes say that a recipient receives undelivered messages "at most once". That holds for prompts carrying a single message. For prompts carrying several messages, v1.1.1 could re-inject the second and later messages after a post-submission crash, as described above. v1.1.2 makes the statement hold in both cases. `docs/releases/v1.1.1.md` carries a matching addendum.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.1.1: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js. Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

Operation records are unchanged: operation schema version 2, as in v1.1.1. No migration runs, and v1.1.1 can read records written by v1.1.2.

The multi-message resume correction is present in the candidate branch (`c0afc44c`). It is one corrective change within the larger roadmap scope, not the definition of this release. Qualification must cover the complete WP-1101–WP-1108 scope on the exact final candidate, including its full test and type gates, package and upgrade checks, independent review, and installed-candidate acceptance. v1.1.1 qualification or evidence from an earlier candidate does not qualify the final v1.1.2 candidate.

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Maturity:** Stable release for Nexus Code v1.1.2, shipped **with known limitations** that the owner accepted explicitly. They are listed in full below, and the [qualification record](v1.1.2-qualification.md) carries the evidence and the open items.

v1.1.2 delivers the WP-1101 to WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0. The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files, and v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2. No `v1.1.2-rc.*` tag was ever published; the candidates that carried those names are superseded.

## What is in this release

- **WP-1101, local OpenTelemetry tracing.** GenAI spans for turns, model requests, tool dispatch and compaction, written locally with payload-free attributes. Trace output is confined to the approved trace directory.
- **WP-1102, flight-recorder credential redaction.** Credential redaction across traces, CLI errors and debug journals.
- **WP-1103, versioned evaluation datasets.** Datasets with separate examples and oracles and regression and benchmark splits; candidate prompts do not carry oracle paths or commands.
- **WP-1104, standalone `nexus eval`.** A packaged command with dataset selection, run count, an isolated home and structured score output. It runs outside the repository checkout.
- **WP-1105, deterministic code evaluators.** AST, build, typecheck, diff-boundary and JSON-repair evaluators and tool-call syntax telemetry (`toolCallSyntax`). **The evaluators are a library: no dataset task uses them yet.** See the limitations below.
- **WP-1106, single-step loop mode.** `--step`, and `/step` in the REPL and the TUI, pause after one agent turn for operator confirmation.
- **WP-1107, bounded tool grammar and provider-specific strict tool schemas.** A bounded schema compiler, plus strict tool schemas for llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama request paths. The 99.5% valid-tool-call target was **not measured** against live providers; see below.
- **WP-1108, dependency modernisation.** The pending Dependabot updates were triaged and merged. `cargo deny` is clean, there are no deprecated npm packages, and a CycloneDX SBOM is generated.
- **Non-progress recovery.** A bounded recovery state machine for repeated unproductive tool calls, with state-based same-step progress and unique tool-call ids ([#398](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/398)).
- **Specialist orchestration and independent review.** Specialist roles with tool allow-lists, an evidence-based review boundary for operation units, and redaction of credential-named keys in review evidence ([#396](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/396), [#401](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/401)).

## Fixed

### A crash-resumed unit no longer receives a multi-message prompt's later messages twice

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

- Impact in v1.1.1: the duplicated message was advisory context only. No message was lost, and no `TurnResult`, verification, or acceptance outcome was affected.
- Regression coverage: the post-prompt crash test in `cli/test/operation_release_review.test.ts` carries two messages and asserts that each appears once in the durable history and is acknowledged once.

### Correction to the v1.1.1 notes

The v1.1.1 notes say that a recipient receives undelivered messages "at most once". That holds for prompts carrying a single message. For prompts carrying several messages, v1.1.1 could re-inject the second and later messages after a post-submission crash. v1.1.2 makes the statement hold in both cases. `docs/releases/v1.1.1.md` carries a matching addendum.

## Known limitations (owner waiver)

Independent reviewers examined the release source and returned REQUEST CHANGES on the WP-1105 evaluator work and on the WP-1107 provider work. The owner decided to ship v1.1.2 with the findings below open, and to fix only one of them (the `typecheck_clean` diagnostic pattern, commit `2dbe565b`). Nothing in this list has been fixed in this release. The review reports are on [PR #402](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/402).

### Not measured

- **Constrained decoding, gate G1.1-4: NOT MET, NOT MEASURED.** The target is at least 99.5% valid tool-call JSON across supported provider endpoints. The provider-specific strict schemas are connected and tested locally with mock servers. No measurement against live llama.cpp, vLLM or Ollama endpoints was made, because the shared gateway resource was held by another release stream. Do not read this release as having met that target.
- **Task quality.** The benchmark fixture checks execution and prompt boundaries, not task-solving or provider quality.

### Provider handling (WP-1107)

- **The server-kind cache never expires or invalidates.** A server kind learned for an endpoint is kept when a later model-list refresh is unreadable (503, bad JSON, dropped connection, 404 or the model not listed). If the server on that endpoint is replaced, the old kind and its strict flag can remain. A gateway kept this way sends the `X-Task-Class` header to a non-gateway server that replaced it on the same endpoint. The rule that standalone local servers do not receive `X-Task-Class` (REQ-PRV-109) therefore holds on the success path and for non-gateway kinds, not in that replacement case.
- **Null normalisation covers well-formed native tool calls only.** Calls that needed JSON repair, and text-mode tool calls, still reach read tracking with `null` optional fields. The normaliser also strips an explicit `null` from every optional property of every tool for all providers, including properties whose schema allows null.
- **Request counting can turn off.** After a transient `/version` failure, or a 404 or missing-model refresh, a retained vLLM kind no longer matches the advertised source, so the agent probably reports that request counting is unavailable.
- **Matrix provenance is not bound to the checkout content.** The matrix runner now verifies the installed archive and the clean checkout commit, but any clean repository at the claimed commit passes.
- **Ollama identity.** A transient `/api/version` failure on a successful refresh still drops the kind to unknown.

### Code evaluators (WP-1105)

- **Fail-open overlay.** Build and typecheck run in the baseline workspace with only candidate edits to `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.rs` and `.py` files overlaid. Edits to any other file (`.go`, `.c`, `.json` and so on) are invisible to the build, so a change in one of those files that breaks the build can pass. Honest changes to such inputs, for example a new JSON module, can fail.
- **Shadowing.** A candidate can still shadow the checker through `node_modules` or an in-repo build helper, because those files are overlaid as source.
- **Large workspaces.** The runner takes two full workspace snapshots even for build-only tasks. A workspace with a very large `node_modules` is refused (5 second traversal deadline, 50,000 entries).
- **No resource limits on evaluator commands** (memory, process count, disk); in-process parsers have no timeout (a 65 MB TypeScript file blocked for about 63 seconds); a command path that resolves outside the workspace through a symlink or `..` runs; `typecheck_clean` reports a benign line shift in a diagnostic as new.
- **`typecheck_clean` recognises only coded diagnostics** (`error TS1234:` or `error[E0123]:`). Checkers that print other formats fail closed whenever the baseline already has errors, and identical recognised configuration errors on both sides (for example TS5057) still pass.
- **Other.** A syntax error in an ambiguous `.js` file that is valid ESM is not caught by `node --check`; a dangling symlink at an overlaid path fails closed with `EEXIST`; the evaluator README is partly stale.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.1.1: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js. Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Upgrade

Operation records are unchanged: operation schema version 2, as in v1.1.1. No migration runs, and v1.1.1 can read records written by v1.1.2.

## Qualification

The [qualification record](v1.1.2-qualification.md) states what was run, on which commit, with which result, and what was not run. In short: the exact source head passed the full local suite and security gates (counts in the record). Independent review of the WP-1105 and WP-1107 work was not an ACCEPT; its findings are the limitations above.

I'd already read that same list through the Entire CLI. It is the 16 open findings on PR #402, with one HIGH. Nothing is merged or tagged.

- **The HIGH (step pause bypass), fixed.** In `--step` mode, a turn with two or more `read_file` calls skipped the pause. I reproduced it, then wrote the test first (`AC1b` in `step_loop.test.ts`) and confirmed it failed. The fix is six lines in `cli/src/agent.ts`: the parallel path now applies the same pause conditions as the sequential path. `step_loop.test.ts` now passes 9/9.

- **The 15 other findings, which I did not fix:** you chose to fix only the HIGH, so I documented them as known limitations in the release notes, labelled as Entire's findings. I reproduced only the HIGH myself. The notable ones:
  - **TUI `/step`:** it runs the turn without a rollback checkpoint, so `/undo` can discard earlier work as well. It also can't be cancelled, saves no session, and reports a blocked turn as success.
  - **Step pause vs stagnation:** the pause overwrites a stagnation stop, so stagnation detection can't advance across `/step` calls.
  - **`--isolated-home`:** it is honoured only when `eval` is the first argument. With a global option in front it is silently ignored and the run uses your real home.
  - **`diff_boundary`:** it can reject a valid patch.
  - **Smaller items:** the trace scope version is hard-coded to 1.1.0, the GBNF compiler is dead code, and redaction is applied in two layers.
  I also corrected the WP-1106 row in the qualification record, which had claimed it simply passed.

<result># Nexus Code worktree inventory for the v1.1.3 Worktrunk-style plan

I read the files at `~/nexus-wt/v112-release` (branch `v1/v112-release`, HEAD `822c08fb`) and compared against `origin/main` (`929afb11`). `origin/main` is 48 commits behind the release branch. The files that matter here are identical on both: `worktree.ts`, `operation_git.ts`, `git_exclude.ts`, `slash/workspace_commands.ts` and `core/app.ts`. The only differences are `catalog.ts` (+1 line), `session_commands.ts`, `repl.ts`, `index.ts`, and `redactDiagnosticForOutput` in `persistence_protection.ts`. I ran no tests, builds or cargo; only git and file reads. All paths below are relative to `cli/src/` unless noted.

## 1. What exists today

There are two separate worktree engines. Neither takes a user-chosen branch name or path.

**A. `WorktreeManager` (`worktree.ts`): one ephemeral "speculative" worktree per task**
- **Path and branch:** worktrees live at `<gitRoot>/.nexus/worktrees/<taskId>` (`getWorktreesBaseDir`, L78). The branch is `nexus/<taskId>`, and the default taskId is `task-<uuid8>`. Both conventions are hard-coded: `hasChanges` (L190), `mergeWorktree` and `discardWorktree` all rebuild `nexus/${taskId}`, not looked up.
- **Git root:** `gitRoot` comes from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (L54). Run from inside a linked worktree, that returns the linked worktree's root, not the main one.
- **Create:** `createWorktree(taskId, startPoint="HEAD")` (L100–137):
  - It calls `ensureGitExclude(gitRoot)` first, then runs `git worktree add -b nexus/<id> <path> <startPoint>`.
  - It refuses if the directory already exists.
  - `startPoint` is passed as an argv element with no validation.
- **List:** `listWorktrees` (L143) parses `git worktree list --porcelain` and keeps only entries whose path starts with the base dir (a bare `startsWith`, with no separator check). Sibling worktrees and the main checkout are invisible to it.
- **Change detection:**
  - `hasChanges` runs `status --porcelain --ignored=matching` plus `rev-list --count`, and returns true if the worktree is unreadable.
  - `hasIgnoredChanges` flags ignored output.
  - `rootHasChanges` checks the root checkout.
- **Merge:** `mergeWorktree` (L240–339) refuses in these cases:
  - ignored output exists (CAND-004);
  - the root checkout is dirty (CAND-004);
  - a validation receipt is required but missing, not PASSED, or whose candidate identity no longer matches (CAND-001..003).

  If it passes, it commits `add -A` in the worktree, runs `merge --no-ff` in the root, and then discards.
- **Discard:** `discardWorktree` runs `worktree remove --force`, falls back to `rm -rf` plus `prune`, then `branch -D`, then `prune`. There is no dirty-state check, so it is destructive.
- **Callers:**
  - `agent.ts` is the main one: `run()` L6795–6872, `mergeActiveWorktree` L1808, `discardActiveWorktree` L1831, and `setWorkspace` L2394/2397/2442 (it refuses `/cd` while a worktree is unresolved).
  - `evaluator.ts` L158–300 makes eval worktrees with a task id and `base_commit`.
  - `core/state.ts` L22 and `core/app.ts` L454 (the `worktrees` command, JSON output) also call it.
- **Lifecycle with `--worktree`:**
  - `Agent.run()` requires a git repo and a usable sandbox (bwrap or docker, L6799–6807). It creates the worktree, switches the workspace to it with the sandbox forced on (`bridgeSandboxSetting` L2471, and the bridge's `requireSandbox`), runs the turn, then decides in `finally`.
  - It auto-merges only if there is a validation receipt, the root is clean, and there is no ignored output.
  - Otherwise it prints "retaining worktree". If there are no changes, it discards.
  - Interactive `runTurn` throws if a worktree is unresolved (L5499).
- **Durable binding:**
  - Task state stores `worktreeBinding {taskId, worktreePath, branch}` (`core/state.ts` L83).
  - Recovery (`state.ts` ~L924) reports consistent, missing, detached or none.
  - The agent re-enters the recorded worktree on recovery (`agent.ts` L1655–1666).

**B. `OperationGit` (`core/operation_git.ts`): opt-in isolation for `nexus operation` runs**
- **Enabling it:** set `git: {isolate: true, baseRef?}` in the operation spec JSON (`operation_cli.ts` L42, L62, L100, L263). There is no CLI flag. A `publish: "pr"` key is rejected fail-closed (DEC-V11-12).
- **Layout:**
  - Base dir is `<repoRoot>/.nexus/worktrees/op-<slug>`, with `integration/` and `units/<slug>` under it (L73–81).
  - Branches are `nexus/op-<key>/integration` and `nexus/op-<key>/<unit-slug>`.
  - `gitSlug` is the first 40 characters of the lowercased, sanitized id plus a sha256 hash of 8 hex characters.
- **Operations:**
  - `ensureIntegrationWorktree` is idempotent and fails closed on a broken branch/worktree pair.
  - `prepareUnit` reuses, restarts or repairs a worktree: `prune --expire now`, `remove --force`, and `branch -D` on restart.
  - `integrate` commits, then does a `--no-ff` merge in the integration worktree, re-runs the verifier on the merged tree, and resets on failure.
- **Hook neutralization:** merges and commits use `mechanicalGitConfig`, which sets a fixed author, `commit.gpgsign=false` and an empty `core.hooksPath` dir at `<baseDir>/no-hooks`, plus `--no-verify`.
- **Retention:**
  - `disposeUnit` and `disposeAllUnits` remove a unit worktree only if `status --porcelain --ignored` is empty.
  - `preservedWorktrees` reports retained ones as "dirty" or "ignored".
  - `operation_runner.ts` L607–614 emits the `WORKTREE_RETAINED` event (declared in `core/operation.ts` L200, documented in `docs/v1.1.0/SPEC.md` L423 and L580).
  - The integration worktree is deliberately kept as the inspection surface.
- **Nothing here is user-facing.** It is internal, driven only by the spec.

**C. Safety and path-confinement code that hard-codes the layout**
- `core/git_exclude.ts` `ensureGitExclude`:
  - It writes `.nexus/.gitignore` containing `*` using O_NOFOLLOW, nlink and `/proc/self/fd` checks.
  - It probes that `.nexus/worktrees/...` is ignored.
  - It best-effort appends `.nexus/`, `.nexus/worktrees/` and `.nexus/flights/` to `info/exclude`.
  - It throws if Git metadata is unverifiable, so worktree creation fails closed.
- `core/persistence_protection.ts`:
  - `isManagedWorktreePath` (L45–86) accepts a recorded worktree path only if it equals `<gitRoot>/.nexus/worktrees/<taskId>`, the branch is `nexus/<taskId>`, the realpath matches, the root and common dir match, and the branch is the current one.
  - `hasValidatedOperationGitPaths` (L123–149) enforces the `.nexus/worktrees/op-*/{integration,units/*}` layout for operation state.
- `core/git_hook_guard.ts` `envWithoutConfiguredHooks`:
  - It disables Git 2.54+ config-declared hooks via `hook.<event>.enabled=false`.
  - It fails closed on Git 2.54 exactly, and is used only by `checkpoint.ts`.
- `core/candidate.ts` computes candidate identity for a worktree. `core/workspace_path.ts` and `safe_fs.ts` provide path-identity and verified-mkdir helpers.

**Rust core.** There is no worktree code. `core/src/git_ops.rs` only does status, diff and log through `git2`. All worktree work shells out to the `git` binary from TypeScript, using `execFileSync` with argv arrays, with no shell and a 300 s timeout in `operation_git`.

## 2. User-facing surface today

| Surface | Detail |
|---|---|
| `nexus run/repl --worktree` | Flag at `index.ts` L320/358/402 and `sidecar.ts` L1148. Sets `config.worktree` (`config.ts` L405, `types.ts` L91). |
| `--authoritative-verifier <cmd>` | Trusted command that gates completion and authorizes automatic merge (`types.ts` L92). |
| `nexus worktrees [-w]` | `index.ts` L977–994. Read-only list of speculative worktrees (task id, branch, path, head). |
| `/worktree [status\|merge\|discard]` | Catalog `slash/catalog.ts` L105, handler `slash/workspace_commands.ts` L116–135. Operates only on the agent's active worktree. REPL equivalent at `repl.ts` L1062–1100; help text at L382. |
| Read-only gating | Duplicated in `repl.ts` `replReadOnlyAllowed` L98 and `sidecar.ts` `readOnlySlashAllowed` L36. Both allow only empty or `status`. |
| `/cd` | `session_commands.ts` L189. Refuses while a worktree is unresolved (via `Agent.setWorkspace`). |
| Other git commands | `/git`, `/diff`, `/stage`, `/commit` and `/checkpoint*` use `git.ts` and `workspace_commands.ts`. `app.ts` L454 exposes the `worktrees` command. |
| Operation spec | `git: {isolate, baseRef}` only. `operation_view.ts` renders the integration branch and worktree. |
| Config and env | There are no worktree-specific config keys or env vars. `PROJECT_ENV_KEYS` (`config.ts` L134–154) does not include any. |
| Docs | Worktree docs are limited to `docs/v1.1.0/GIT_AWARE_OPERATIONS.md` (accurate, status reconciled 2026-10-31), `SPEC.md`, `DECISIONS.md` and `STATUS.md`. `USER_MANUAL.md`, `CLIENT_GUIDE.md`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` do not mention worktrees. `/help` is the command reference. |

## 3. Seams for a new worktree workflow

- **New module:** a new `cli/src/worktree_cli.ts` or `slash/worktree_commands.ts` would fit the existing shape. `git.ts` is already a place for pure git helpers.
- **Slash registration (three edits):**
  - Add a `SlashSpec {name, usage, summary, aliases?, cancellable?}` in `slash/catalog.ts`.
  - Add a handler to a `*_HANDLERS` map, merged in `slash/router.ts` L8.
  - Add the read-only allow rules in both `replReadOnlyAllowed` and `readOnlySlashAllowed`.
- **What the router and sidecar do for you:**
  - The router returns `reply(...)` or a turn. It never writes to stdout, and it strips escapes.
  - The sidecar redacts output with `formatSafeSidecarText` (`sidecar.ts` L1068) and caps it at `MAX_SLASH_OUTPUT`.
  - Non-`cancellable` commands cannot be cancelled mid-run (`sidecar.ts` L361).
  - The Rust TUI takes its completion list from the `hello` catalogue, so there is no hard-coded slash list in `core/` (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui/slash.rs` only parses input).
- **Two more call sites:** the readline REPL has a separate if/else chain (`repl.ts` ~L1062) that must be mirrored. The Commander subcommands in `index.ts` (`program.command(...)`, ~43 of them) use `-w/--workspace` and picocolors, with `safeTerminal` for output.
- **Config:**
  - Operator settings come from `~/.config/nexus/config.env`, plus structured JSON at `~/.config/nexus/config.json` (version 1, 64 KiB cap, non-symlink; validated by `readOperatorOperationPolicy`, errors deferred to doctor).
  - `effectiveSetting` precedence is: shell env, then allowlisted project `.env`, then `config.env`, then the process environment.
  - A project `.env` can set only `PROJECT_ENV_KEYS` or `NEXUS_PROJECT_*`. A project `nexus.config.json` is "never trusted as operator policy" (`config.ts` L81).
  - A repo-level hooks file therefore has no existing home. Any such file would be a new, untrusted-by-default input.
- **Trust and approval:**
  - Workspace trust (`workspace_trust.ts`) is a store at `~/.config/nexus/trusted_workspaces.json`. It gates project MCP and plugins, and is always false in read-only mode.
  - `ApprovalPolicy` (`core/approval_policy.ts`) governs write and exec. Review mode always prompts; auto mode does not prompt for exec; fullAccess bypasses.
  - There is a direct approval precedent in `/test` (`workspace_commands.ts` L161–208): a repo-discovered command is shown with its digest and script, and approved through `host.requestApproval("verifier", …)`, then run via `bridge.executeTool("run_command")`, which is sandboxed.
  - `core/authority.ts` handles tool admission and read-only command allowlisting. The bwrap/docker wrappers are in `sandbox.ts`.
  - Plugins (`plugins.ts`) load from `~/.nexus/plugins` and `~/.config/nexus/plugins`, and from the workspace only when trusted.
- **Redaction:** `safeTerminal` (`ui.ts` L28), `formatReplDiagnostic` (`repl.ts` L72), `formatSafeSidecarText`, and `redactForPersistence` / `redactDiagnosticForOutput` (`core/persistence_protection.ts`). Branch names, paths and hook output all need to go through these.
- **Concurrency conventions (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`):** these are for agents developing the repo, not runtime features. Claims live in `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` (atomic `mkdir`), including `SUITE`, `GATEWAY` and `FILE_<path>` hot-file claims. Tests need an isolated HOME, never `pkill -f`, and full suites run on a snapshot. Leave push, tag and publish to the owner.

## 4. Constraints a new feature must meet

- **No new dependencies.**
  - The CLI has four runtime dependencies: commander, dotenv, ora and picocolors.
  - The Rust crate set is small, and `deny.toml` allows only Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2/3, ISC, Unicode-3.0, Zlib and MPL-2.0.
  - `unmaintained = "all"` and `yanked = "deny"` are in force.
  - Gate G1.1-5 (`docs/v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md` L59, L148–155) is described as inviolable: no deprecated or unmaintained dependency, and 0 CodeQL alerts and 0 compiler warnings.
  - Reflink copying must therefore use `node:fs` (`copyFile` with `COPYFILE_FICLONE` / `cp`) or the system `cp --reflink`, not a new crate or package.
- **Gates in `scripts/security_gates.sh` (run by `make test` and `make security-scan`):** `npm audit` at high/critical; `cargo deny check licenses advisories` (or `cargo audit`); a secret-pattern grep over tracked files excluding `cli/test`, `cli/dist`, `scripts` and `docs/reviews/evidence/*/repro/**`; `git diff --check`; and a Gate 4 grep over `README.md`, `quickstart.md` and `docs/*.md` for forbidden identifiers (`t5820|engineering/b0|A770|18010|parity with`).
- **CI-only checks:** `scripts/check_deprecated_lock.mjs` and `scripts/check_notices.mjs`. CI also runs `sync-version --check`, `check_requirements.mjs` and `generate_sbom.sh`. `npm ci` uses a lockfile, so any package change breaks the SBOM and notices.
- **`scripts/doc_commands.mjs`** extracts every fenced `nexus …` line from `README.md`, `quickstart.md`, `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `docs/CLIENT_GUIDE.md` and `docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md` and executes them against the binary. Documenting a new subcommand means it must parse and run.
- **Rust versus TypeScript:**
  - `core/` holds the tool bridge (`harness-core`) and `nexus-tui`. It has no knowledge of worktrees, and the TUI learns commands from the sidecar catalogue.
  - Everything worktree-related is TypeScript in `cli/`.
  - A TypeScript-only feature needs no change to `core/Cargo.toml` and no new Rust build.
- **Packaging:**
  - `package-linux.sh` bundles `cli/dist` and a `npm ci --omit=dev` tree, so only production dependencies ship.
  - `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `npm ci` then the build.
  - `Makefile verify-reproducibility` requires byte-identical archives.
  - `cli/dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore` L65), so the CI check `git diff --exit-code -- cli/dist` passes trivially.
  - The package is Linux x86_64 only.
- **Test conventions:**

<result># Worktrunk (`wt`) survey for Nexus Code integration

Sources are `gh api` reads of `max-sixty/worktrunk` at `main` and v0.81.0, plus the crates.io API. Nothing was cloned, built or run. I did not fetch worktrunk.dev. I used the generated mirror of its docs in `skills/worktrunk/reference/*.md`, which a `readme_sync` test keeps in step with `src/cli/mod.rs`. Source claims below come from `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/shell_exec.rs`, `src/commands/command_approval.rs`, `src/config/approvals.rs`, `src/commands/step/copy_ignored.rs` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## 1. Command surface

Top-level enum in `src/cli/mod.rs`: `Switch`, `List`, `Remove`, `Merge`, a hidden deprecated `Select`, `Step`, `Hook`, `Config`, an internal pair, and `Custom` (`wt <name>` falls through to a `wt-<name>` binary).

- **`wt switch [BRANCH]`** switches to a branch's worktree and creates it if missing.
  - Flags: `-c/--create`, `-b/--base`, `--path` (experimental), `-x/--execute <prog> -- args`, `--clobber`, `--no-cd`, `--no-hooks`, `--yes`, `--format json`.
  - Shortcuts: `^` (default branch), `@`, `-`, `pr:N`, `mr:N`, a PR URL, or `origin/x`.
  - No argument opens the skim picker, with `--branches`, `--remotes` and `--prs`. It has 8 preview tabs (diff, working, committed, log, remote, summary, pr, comments).
- **`wt list`** shows worktrees with status symbols, ahead/behind, diff stats and age.
  - `--full` adds CI and LLM-summary columns; `--branches` and `--remotes` add rows without worktrees.
  - `--format=json` uses a "Schema 2". `wt list statusline` has a Claude Code mode.
- **`wt remove [BRANCH...]`** removes the worktree and deletes the branch if it is integrated.
  - Flags: `-f` (dirty worktree), `-D` (unmerged branch), `--no-delete-branch`, `--foreground`, `--format json`.
  - Integration is checked six ways: same commit, ancestor, empty three-dot diff, equal trees, simulated merge, patch-id.
- **`wt merge [TARGET]`** runs the commit, squash, rebase, pre-merge, fast-forward, pre-remove, cleanup, post-hooks pipeline.
  - Flags: `--branch`, `--no-squash`, `--no-commit`, `--no-rebase`, `--no-remove`, `--no-ff`, `--stage all|tracked|none`.
  - It never fetches.
- **`wt step`** holds the building blocks:
  - `commit`, `squash`, `rebase`, `push` and `diff`.
  - `copy-ignored`, `eval` and `for-each`.
  - `prune`, which has `--dry-run` and `--min-age` (default 1d).
  - Experimental: `promote`, `relocate` and `tether` (kills a process tree when its worktree is removed).
- **`wt hook <type>`** runs hooks on demand: `--foreground`, `--dry-run`, `user:`/`project:` filters, `--KEY=val` overrides, `-- args`.
- **`wt config`**:
  - `shell install|uninstall|init|show`, `create [--project]`, `show`, `update`.
  - `approvals list|add|clear` (`list --format=json` reports whether an unattended run would stop for approval).
  - `alias show|dry-run`.
  - `state cache|default-branch|logs|marker|vars|clear`.
  - `plugins claude|codex|opencode|pi|omp install|uninstall`.
- **Aliases**: `[aliases]` in either config file, run as `wt <name>`. `[[aliases.NAME]]` blocks make multi-step pipelines.
- Globals: `-C`, `-v/-vv`, `--config-set <toml>`, and `WORKTRUNK_*` environment overrides.

## 2. Configuration model

- **User config** is TOML at `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml`, honouring `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. It holds `worktree-path`, `[commit.generation]`, `[list]`, `[switch.picker]`, `[step.copy-ignored]`, hooks, aliases and per-repo `[projects."github.com/o/r"]` overrides.
- **System config** has one path per platform, and `WORKTRUNK_SYSTEM_CONFIG_PATH` overrides it.
- **Approvals** are in `~/.config/worktrunk/approvals.toml`.
- **Project config** is `.config/wt.toml`, committed and shared. It holds hooks, `[list] url`, `[forge]`, `[aliases]`, `[step.copy-ignored] exclude`, and `[commit.generation] template-append` only.
- **Precedence**: `--config-set`, then `WORKTRUNK_*` env, then the `[projects.*]` entry, then the global key. Hooks, aliases and copy excludes accumulate rather than replace.
- **Path template**: the default is `{{ repo_path }}/../{{ repo }}.{{ branch | sanitize }}`. Template variables are `repo_path`, `repo`, `owner`, `remote_repo` and `branch`.
- **Template engine**: MiniJinja 3.
  - Hook variables: `branch`, `worktree_path`, `commit`, `upstream`, `base`, `target`, `pr_number`, `default_branch`, `primary_worktree_path`, `cwd`, `hook_type`, `args` and `vars.*`.
  - Filters: `sanitize`, `sanitize_db`, `sanitize_hash`, `hash`, `hash_port` (10000-19999), `dirname`, `basename`, `codename(n)`.
  - Functions: `worktree_path_of_branch()` and `expected_worktree_path_of_branch()`.
  - Variables are shell-escaped automatically.
- **Per-branch state** lives in git config as `worktrunk.state.<branch>.vars.<key>`, with `markers` and a cached default branch alongside. Caches, logs and a trash directory go under `.git/wt/`. Squash backups go to `refs/wt-backup/<branch>`.
- **`.worktreeinclude`** has gitignore syntax, and a file is copied only if it is both gitignored and listed. Without the file, all gitignored files are copied. `--require-include` makes that a no-op instead.
- **Copy-ignored** (`src/commands/step/copy_ignored.rs`, `copy.rs`, `reflink-copy` crate):
  - It reflinks on APFS, btrfs, XFS and ReFS, and does a full copy on ext4 and NTFS.
  - Existing destination files are skipped, and `--force` overwrites them.
  - Mtimes are preserved so cargo does not rebuild a copied `target/`.
  - Built-in excludes cover VCS metadata, `.worktrees/` and `.entire/`.
  - The docs report a 14 GB `target/` copying in about 20 s with roughly zero extra disk.
  - Python venvs are not copyable, because they contain absolute paths.

## 3. Hooks and security

| Event | Blocking `pre-*` | Background `post-*` |
|---|---|---|
| switch | `pre-switch` | `post-switch` |
| create | `pre-start` | `post-start` |
| commit | `pre-commit` | `post-commit` |
| merge | `pre-merge` | `post-merge` |
| remove | `pre-remove` | `post-remove` |

- A `pre-*` failure aborts the operation. `post-*` output goes to `.git/wt/logs/`.
- Hook forms: a string, a named table (keys run concurrently), or `[[hook]]` blocks (sequential steps, with concurrency inside a step).
- Hooks run under `sh -c` on Unix and Git Bash on Windows (`src/shell_exec.rs`).
- Foreground `pre-*` hooks inherit stdin. From v0.81 hooks no longer receive JSON on stdin.
- **Trust model**:
  - Project hooks and project aliases need first-run approval. The prompt shows the raw templates, and approval is stored per project id plus exact template string (`is_command_approved(project_id, template)`).
  - Any change to a command re-prompts. Declining skips all project commands for that run.
  - `--yes` approves for one run without saving, and `wt config approvals add --yes` saves.
  - User hooks, user aliases and `--execute` need no approval.
  - A project file may only append to the LLM prompt (`template-append`, itself approval-gated). It cannot set the LLM command.
- **Gaps for Nexus**:
  - Approval is interactive-first, which is awkward for unattended agents.
  - Project config is read from the worktree the command runs in, so a checked-out branch can change it.
  - The approval key is a repo identity, not a hash of the whole file.

  - Squash backs up swept-in working-tree changes to `refs/wt-backup/<branch>`.

- **LLM messages**: `[commit.generation] command` is an arbitrary user command. It receives a templated prompt on stdin and prints the message.

- **cd mechanism**: a shell function named `wt` (templates in `templates/{bash.sh,zsh.zsh,fish.fish,nushell.nu,powershell.ps1}`) creates a temp "cd file" and runs `command wt`. If the file is non-empty, it runs `builtin cd`.

  - A `/wt-diff` pane (`register.tsx`) is Claude Code only.

- **Library**: `worktrunk` is on crates.io, 154 versions, MIT OR Apache-2.0. `src/lib.rs` says "The library API is not stable". Every release in the changelog lists breaking library changes.

A `default-features = false` library build avoids the TUI stack but still pulls minijinja, rayon and regex.

| Option | No new runtime dependency | SBOM and immutable-tag packaging | Offline | Hook risk | Upstream churn | Maintenance | Meets "worktrunk functionality" |

| **E** native core plus optional `wt` pass-through | Yes | Clean | Yes | Native part under Nexus's trust model | Limited to the pass-through | Medium | Best |

   - Read `.config/wt.toml` and `.worktreeinclude`.
   - Support a subset of the template syntax.
2. **Phase 2 is a thin A layer.**
   - It detects `wt` on PATH.
   - It runs `wt list --format=json` and `wt config approvals list --format=json` (read-only).
   - It exposes the user's own aliases and the picker through a `/wt` pass-through.

Reasons:
- C and D break the gates and tie Nexus to an API that its author says is unstable.
- A alone fails the user expectation and the offline, strict-trust story.
- Nexus already has the worktree and operation machinery, and the high-value logic is plain git plus a small template engine.

1. **Branch-addressed `switch --create/--base/remove`** with `^`, `@` and `-` shortcuts and branch-or-path resolution.
2. **Path template**, with `sanitize`, `hash_port` and `codename`, and the default `repo.branch` sibling layout.
3. **Copy-ignored with `.worktreeinclude`** and reflink via `cp --reflink=auto`. This is the biggest win for parallel agents (`target/`, `node_modules/`).
4. **`list` with status** from one `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` call, ahead/behind, and integration status, plus JSON.
5. **Merge-and-clean**: squash, rebase, fast-forward only, remove, plus the `refs/wt-backup` safety ref.
6. **`prune` of integrated branches**, with a minimum-age guard.
7. **`post-start` and `pre-merge` hooks**, under Nexus's own trust gate (see risks).
8. **Per-branch `vars`** and an activity marker, which fit Nexus session state.

Defer:
- The skim picker and the preview tabs.
- CI status, which needs forge CLIs.
- LLM commit messages and summaries, until routed through Nexus's own providers.
- `promote`, `relocate`, `tether`.
- The cross-shell cd wrapper (a TypeScript harness can chdir itself).

## Risks

- **Hook execution**: do not honour `.config/wt.toml` hooks implicitly. Require a hash of the command template plus project identity, stored outside the repository. Fail closed when there is no TTY or approval, and never let a branch checkout introduce unreviewed commands.
- **Schema drift**: worktrunk breaks its templates and JSON between releases. Support a documented subset, version-gate the adapter, and test against recorded `wt list --format=json` fixtures.
- **Data safety**: never force-remove untracked files. Take worktrunk's `-f` and `-D` split, and make cleanup a separate action.

- **Branch config trust**: a project `worktree-path` pointing outside the repository needs the same trust treatment.
- **Name collision**: `wt` clashes with Windows Terminal, which is why worktrunk ships `git-wt`. Detect by `--version` output, not by name.
- **Shared git state**: parallel worktree operations race on git config and locks. Keep the single-writer discipline Nexus's operation machinery already has.
- **Scope**: exact-parity expectations ("worktrunk functionality") will grow. State the supported subset and its config keys explicitly.

# Nexus Code v1.1.3 Plan

**Status:** Draft for owner review. **Base:** `main` after the v1.1.2 merge and tag.
**Scope (owner, 2026-11-04):** (1) resolve every open finding from v1.1.2; (2) add Worktrunk functionality in the best-integrated way.

## 1. Principles

- Close findings with the fix first, the regression test red first, and an independent review per work package. Findings are closed with evidence, never by editing the finding.
- No new runtime dependency (gate G1.1-5: zero deprecated packages, `cargo deny`, SBOM, notices). Anything Worktrunk-shaped must be built on Node, git and the system `cp`.
- Project-supplied commands are untrusted input. Nothing a repository file declares runs without an approval that lives outside the repository.
- One exact-head gate per release candidate, run with the CI fixture variables set so `make test` runs through, in a clean worktree with its own `npm ci`.

## 2. Findings ledger

Sources: my independent reviews on PR #402 (WP-1105 evaluators, WP-1107 provider work), Entire trail 145 (15 open findings after the `--step` HIGH was fixed in v1.1.2), Entire trail 140, and the known limitations in `docs/releases/v1.1.2.md`. ## 3. Worktrunk integration

### 3.1 What Worktrunk is (survey, 2026-11-04)
A Rust CLI `wt` (v0.81.0, pre-1.0, MIT OR Apache-2.0, about 12 releases in 83 days with breaking changes in each). Branch-addressed `switch/list/remove/merge`, a configurable path template (default sibling `repo.branch`), `copy-ignored` build-cache sharing with `.worktreeinclude`, hooks (`pre-start/post-start/pre-merge/...`), per-branch variables, aliases, PR checkout, CI status, LLM commit messages, a picker, and Claude Code and Codex plugins. It shells out to `git`. Its library crate is declared unstable.

### 3.2 Decision: native subset first, optional pass-through second
| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| A. Adapter only (`wt` on PATH) | Not enough alone: no offline or trust story under Nexus's control, and it only works for users who install `wt`. Kept as phase 2. |
| B. Native subset in TypeScript | **Phase 1.** Built on Nexus's own git handling. No dependency, no packaging change. |
| C. Embed the `worktrunk` crate | **Rejected.** About 100 new crates, MSRV 1.98, unstable API; breaks G1.1-5 and the SBOM. |
| D. Vendor or fork | **Rejected.** Large, fast-moving, and it would tie the release cadence to upstream. |
| E. B plus an optional `wt` pass-through | **Chosen.** Phase 2 adds a read-only adapter that detects `wt` by `--version` output. |

Licence: reimplementing ideas needs no licence. Do not copy code. Credit Worktrunk in the docs, and do not reuse its name for the feature. The Nexus command is `nexus worktree` (alias `nexus wt` only if no collision is detected at install; `wt` collides with Windows Terminal).

### 3.3 Design constraints from the Nexus inventory
1. **A new managed worktree kind.** The existing `isManagedWorktreePath` and `hasValidatedOperationGitPaths` accept only `<gitRoot>/.nexus/worktrees/<taskId>` on `nexus/<taskId>`. User-named worktrees at a path template such as `../repo.feature` need their own state kind and validators. Do not loosen the existing ones.
2. **Anchor on the git common dir.** The repo root must come from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, not `--show-toplevel`, so Nexus run inside a linked worktree finds the main checkout and sees all siblings. This also fixes a latent bug in `WorktreeManager`.
3. **Registry.** Named worktrees are recorded in `<git-common-dir>/nexus/worktrees.json` (atomic write, no symlinks, 64 KiB cap), so `list`, `remove` and state recovery do not depend on the path layout.
4. **Safe removal.** `remove` refuses a dirty worktree (including untracked and ignored files) and an unmerged branch unless `--force` / `--delete-unmerged` is given. Do not reuse `WorktreeManager.discardWorktree` (it is `--force` plus `branch -D`).
5. **Git hooks off during creation.** Creating a worktree runs `post-checkout`; use the existing `envWithoutConfiguredHooks` suppression (extend it to cover Git 2.54 correctly) for every Nexus-initiated git call.
6. **Config without a TOML dependency.** Operator config is JSON (`~/.config/nexus/config.json`, version 1, existing validator). Reading Worktrunk's `.config/wt.toml` and `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml` uses a small strict TOML-subset reader (tables, strings, string arrays; anything else is an error, never guessed). It is read-only interoperability, not a requirement.
7. **Read-only gating in both places.** Every new slash command must be added to `replReadOnlyAllowed` (repl.ts) and `readOnlySlashAllowed` (sidecar.ts) with a test; mutating subcommands are refused in read-only mode.
8. **Docs gates.** Fenced `nexus …` examples are executed by `scripts/doc_commands.mjs`; they must parse. Gate 4 scans only top-level `docs/*.md`.

### 3.4 Work packages
**WP-1310 Core: named worktrees**
- `nexus worktree switch <branch> [-c] [--base B] [--no-copy]`, `list [--json]`, `remove <branch>... [--force] [--delete-unmerged]`, `path <branch>`. Branch shortcuts: `^` default branch, `@` current, `-` previous. Accept a worktree path wherever a branch is accepted.
- Path template: default `{{ repo_path }}/../{{ repo }}.{{ branch | sanitize }}`; variables `repo_path`, `repo`, `owner`, `branch`; filters `sanitize`, `hash_port`, `codename`; implemented by a small expression evaluator (no template dependency). A rendered path outside the repository's parent directory, or into an existing non-worktree directory, is refused unless the operator config allows it.
- `list` from one `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` call per worktree plus `rev-list --left-right --count`: dirty, ahead and behind the default branch, integrated (same commit, ancestor, empty three-dot diff, equal tree, patch-id), age, agent marker. JSON schema versioned from day one.
- Slash commands `/worktree switch|list|remove` (the existing `/worktree status|merge|discard` keep working), CLI subcommand, sidecar catalogue entry, completion in the TUI, read-only rules, redaction of branch names and paths.
- `nexus run --worktree` keeps its behaviour. A new `--worktree-branch <name>` creates a named worktree for the task instead of `nexus/<taskId>` (opt-in, same sandbox requirement).

**WP-1311 Shared build caches**
- `nexus worktree copy-ignored [--from B] [--to B] [--force] [--dry-run]` and the automatic step in `switch -c`. Source set: files that are both gitignored and listed in `.worktreeinclude`. Default is include-only; the "copy every ignored file" mode needs `--all-ignored` because it can copy `.env` secrets into every worktree.
- Implementation: `fs.cp` with `COPYFILE_FICLONE` where supported, `cp --reflink=auto` fallback, plain copy elsewhere; preserve mtimes (so cargo does not rebuild a copied `target/`); skip existing files unless `--force`; exclude `.git`, `.nexus`, `.entire`, nested worktrees; refuse symlinks that leave the tree; cap on count and bytes with a clear error.
- Never copy Python virtualenvs (absolute paths); say so.

**WP-1312 Merge and clean**
- `nexus worktree merge [target] [--no-squash] [--no-rebase] [--no-remove]`: commit (optionally LLM-generated through Nexus's configured provider, never an external command by default), squash, rebase onto target, fast-forward only, then remove the worktree and branch. Back up swept-in working-tree changes to `refs/nexus-backup/<branch>` before squashing. Rebase conflicts stay open in the worktree with a clear message. Uses the existing validation receipt gate (CAND-001..004) when a verifier is configured.
- `nexus worktree prune [--dry-run] [--min-age 1d]`: remove worktrees whose branch is integrated, with the minimum-age guard.

**WP-1313 Hooks under Nexus's trust model**
- Supported events first: `post-start` (after create) and `pre-merge` (blocking). Others later.
- Sources: operator config (trusted) and project `.config/wt.toml`/`.nexus/worktree.json` (untrusted). Project hooks run only after an approval recorded outside the repository (`~/.config/nexus/worktree_approvals.json`) keyed by repository identity, hook name and a hash of the exact command template. Any change re-prompts. No TTY or no approval: skip and say so; never run silently. Never executed with `--yes`-style bypass in unattended or read-only mode.
- Execution goes through the existing `run_command` bridge so the sandbox and approval policy apply, with the same digest-and-script approval display as `/test`. Output is redacted and bounded.
- A branch checkout cannot introduce an unreviewed command: the approval key includes the template hash, and project config is read from the primary checkout, not from the worktree being created.

**WP-1314 Per-branch state and agent markers**
- `nexus worktree vars get|set|clear` stored in the registry (not git config). Hook templates can read `vars`.
- Activity marker (idle/working/waiting) written by the sidecar for the worktree its session runs in, shown in `list`.

**WP-1315 Optional `wt` pass-through (phase 2)**
- Detect `wt` by running `wt --version` and checking the product string; minimum version pin; never bundle it.
- `/wt <args>` forwards to the user's `wt` (read-only subcommands allowed in read-only mode: `list`, `config show`), and `nexus worktree list --source wt` merges `wt list --format=json` after validating it against a recorded schema fixture. A schema mismatch degrades to a warning, never to a guess.
- `wt` aliases and the picker are reachable only through this pass-through.

**Deferred beyond v1.1.3:** the skim-style picker, CI status columns (forge CLIs), PR checkout (`pr:N`, needs `gh`; reconsider after WP-1310), `relocate/promote/tether`, a shell `cd` wrapper (the harness changes its own directory), exposing worktree tools to the model.

## A. Code

**A1. Does 822c08fb fix the parallel-read branch? Yes.**
- The new check sits at `agent.ts:6264-6268` (at c817c031), after `persistProgress` (6262) and before `endStep(); continue;` (6269-6270).
- It mirrors the sequential pause at 6362-6366.
- The `read_file` pair goes through the parallel branch because `READ_ONLY_TOOLS` contains `read_file` (708-709) and the branch condition is at 6217.

**A2. Every path to the next loop iteration.** All line numbers are at c817c031. Each is a `continue` in the main `while` unless noted.

| Location | Path | Model request made? | Tools executed? | Skips the --step pause? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6044-6045 | Reply cut off at the output limit. Fires once in a row (`previousReplyTruncated`). | Yes | No ("nothing from it ran") | Yes | Legitimate non-cycle |
| 6077-6078 | Provider rejected the request for capacity. Compacts messages and retries once (`capacityRetryAttempted`). | Request failed | No | Yes | Legitimate. The compaction touches history, not the workspace. |
| 6166-6167 | Dropped malformed or unknown tool call, so the model gets a notice. | Yes | No | Yes | Legitimate |
| 6172-6173 | Queued steering, applied next step. | Yes | No | Yes | Legitimate |
| 6187-6188 | Empty reply. Fires once in a row (`previousReplyEmpty`). | Yes | No | Yes | Legitimate |
| 6205-6206 | Open acceptance requirements. Up to `maxCompletionNudges` times, and only when `budget` is set. | Yes | No | Yes | Legitimate |
| 6269-6270 | Parallel reads. | Yes | Yes | Not any more | Fixed |

- **Why the first six are not defects.** None of them runs a tool in that iteration, so none can mutate the workspace before the pause.
  - A tool-executing iteration always reaches a pause or terminates. That covers the sequential tail (6362), the parallel branch (now), `TASK_COMPLETED_TOOL`, and the breaks for interruption, abort and failure.
  - So in `--step`, at most one tool cycle runs per `runTurn`.
- **What these paths do allow.** They can issue several tool-less model requests before the tool cycle and its pause. That is bounded by the once-in-a-row flags, the nudge cap and `maxTotalSteps`. It does not violate "one model/tool cycle". Entire's suggestion of a "shared cycle boundary reached by every continuation path" would be stricter than that. I'd record it as a v1.1.3 design question, not a blocker.
- **Loop-top breaks.** The checks at 5696-5717 are break paths, not continues.
- **`continue` at 6242.** It belongs to the inner `for` over tool calls (the refusal path). It reaches the pause at 6362.
- **Text-mode tool calls.** These parse into `parsed.toolCalls` and take the same branches. There are no other `continue`s in the loop.

**A3. Is the new pause condition correct?** Yes, with one nit (N1).
- `modelStop` cannot be set by the parallel branch, so `=== "NONE"` always holds.
- `interruption`, `inferenceFailure` and `persistenceFailure` are never set in that branch either.
- The extra `!signal.aborted` is needed. The sequential path has no such check at the pause, but it breaks earlier on abort (6349-6354). In the parallel branch an abort during `Promise.all` falls to `endStep(); continue`, and the loop-top check at 5703 interrupts. That is correct.
- **Skipped `endStep()`.** The new `break` skips the same things the sequential pause skips.
  - `pendingRecoveryNote` is dropped.
  - `tracker.evaluateStep` does not run.
  - `currentStep++` does not run.
  - This is the existing Entire finding `01M6KXHHESMA` (medium), documented as a limitation.
  - `persistProgress` has already run at 6262, so durable state is saved.

**A4. Is AC1b a real regression test? Yes.**
- Reply 1 has two `read_file` calls, so it takes the parallel branch.
- Without the fix: `endStep(); continue` leads to request 2, which writes `after-reads.txt`. Then the sequential pause fires. That gives 2 provider requests and an existing file, and the first assertion fails with the exact observed message ("only 1 provider request").
- The observed RED failure also proves the test reaches the parallel branch, so it cannot pass vacuously. If it had taken the sequential path, it would have been green before the fix.
- Gaps:
  - It does not assert that both tool results are in history.
  - It does not cover `batch_read` or mixed read-only batches.
  - It does not cover the stagnation case (N1).

### Code nit

**N1. Possible regression in the parallel branch, for `--step` only.**
- `refuse()` (5878) and `observe()` can set `stopReason = "STAGNATION_DETECTED"` inside the parallel branch.
- Before the fix, `endStep(); continue` let the loop-top `if (stopReason) break;` (5696) keep that reason.
- With the fix, line 6265 overwrites it with `STEP_PAUSED`. The sequential path already does this (Entire's `01M6KXHHESMA`), but the parallel path did not.

- If you won't touch the code now, say in the notes that the overwrite applies to both branches (see D1). I'd lean toward taking the one-condition fix, but only if a new exact-head gate is acceptable. Otherwise ship as documented.

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Maturity:** Release notes for Nexus Code v1.1.2, which ships **with known limitations** that the owner accepted explicitly. They are listed in full below, and the [qualification record](v1.1.2-qualification.md) carries the evidence and the open items. The tag is created after the release pull request merges; these notes describe the source that is tagged.

v1.1.2 delivers the WP-1101 to WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0, with WP-1107 delivered in reduced form (see below). The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files, and v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2. No `v1.1.2-rc.*` tag was ever published; the candidates that carried those names are superseded.

## What is in this release

- **WP-1101, local OpenTelemetry tracing.** GenAI spans for turns, model requests, tool dispatch and compaction, written locally with payload-free attributes. Trace output is confined to the approved trace directory.
- **WP-1102, flight-recorder credential redaction.** Credential redaction across traces, CLI errors and debug journals.
- **WP-1103, versioned evaluation datasets.** Datasets with separate examples and oracles and regression and benchmark splits; candidate prompts do not carry oracle paths or commands.
- **WP-1104, standalone `nexus eval`.** A packaged command with dataset selection, run count, an isolated home and structured score output. It runs outside the repository checkout.
- **WP-1105, deterministic code evaluators.** AST, build, typecheck, diff-boundary and JSON-repair evaluators and tool-call syntax telemetry (`toolCallSyntax`). **The evaluators are a library: no dataset task uses them yet.** See the limitations below.
- **WP-1106, single-step loop mode.** `--step`, and `/step` in the REPL and the TUI, pause after one agent turn for operator confirmation.
- **WP-1107, bounded tool schemas (reduced scope).** A bounded schema compiler for the four harness tools, and strict function schemas on the **vLLM request path only**. llama.cpp and Ollama requests keep their native tool schemas: no grammar or format constraint is sent for them, and the hybrid reasoning grammars from the roadmap are not implemented. The 99.5% valid-tool-call target was **not measured** against live providers; see below.
- **WP-1108, dependency modernisation.** The pending Dependabot updates were triaged and merged. `cargo deny` is clean, there are no deprecated npm packages, and a CycloneDX SBOM is generated.
- **Non-progress recovery.** A bounded recovery state machine for repeated unproductive tool calls, with state-based same-step progress and unique tool-call ids ([#398](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/398)).
- **Specialist orchestration and independent review.** Specialist roles with tool allow-lists, an evidence-based review boundary for operation units, and redaction of credential-named keys in review evidence ([#396](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/396), [#401](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/401)).

## Fixed

### `--step` now pauses after a cycle of parallel `read_file` calls

In `--step` mode, when the model returned two or more `read_file` calls in one turn, the parallel-read path ended the step without applying the single-step pause, so the run could issue further model requests and execute later edits before returning. The parallel path now pauses like the sequential path, except that a stop already set during that cycle (for example stagnation) is reported instead of being replaced by the pause. Replies that run no tool (retries, nudges, notices) do not pause. Two regression tests were written first and failed before their fixes: `AC1b` in `cli/test/step_loop.test.ts` (the pause after parallel reads) and a stagnation case in `cli/test/nonprogress_recovery.test.ts` (the stop is not hidden by the pause). This was found by Entire's automated review of PR #402 and reproduced.

### A crash-resumed unit no longer receives a multi-message prompt's later messages twice

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

docs/v1.1.3/FINDINGS.md:1:# v1.1.3 findings ledger
docs/v1.1.3/FINDINGS.md:3:Every row ends as FIXED (commit and test), WITHDRAWN (evidence) or DEFERRED (owner decision). Updated per closed item. Source of truth for the v1.1.3 release acceptance.
docs/v1.1.3/FINDINGS.md:24:| 145 | low | `01M6KXHHJ3VQ` | cli/src/core/tool_grammar.ts:12-100 | WP-1303 | The 100-line GBNF compiler (`generateToolArgumentsGbnf` / `generateRegisteredToolArgumentGrammars`) has no runtime caller. Only `GBNF_TOOL_ALLOWLIST` is imported, by `tool_grammar_provider.ts`, and the Trail defers provider grammar to 1.1.3. This ships dead code that has only its own tests. Keep the allowlist and land the compiler with its consumer. | OPEN |
docs/v1.1.3/PLAN.md:1:# Nexus Code v1.1.3 Plan
docs/v1.1.3/PLAN.md:53:- Keep the findings ledger in `docs/v1.1.3/FINDINGS.md`, updated per closed item with the commit.
docs/v1.1.3/PLAN.md:119:**Deferred beyond v1.1.3:** the skim-style picker, CI status columns (forge CLIs), PR checkout (`pr:N`, needs `gh`; reconsider after WP-1310), `relocate/promote/tether`, a shell `cd` wrapper (the harness changes its own directory), exposing worktree tools to the model.
docs/v1.1.3/PLAN.md:128:## 5. Acceptance (v1.1.3)
docs/v1.1.3/PLAN.md:138:2. **Project hooks.** Run project-declared hooks after a recorded approval (recommended) versus operator-config hooks only in v1.1.3.
- No new runtime dependency, no SBOM component change, `cargo deny` and `npm audit` clean.

## 6. Open decisions for the owner
1. **Named worktree location.** Default sibling layout `../repo.branch` (Worktrunk-compatible, outside the repository) versus staying under `.nexus/worktrees/` (safer for confinement, not compatible with existing Worktrunk worktrees). Recommended: sibling layout, opt-in through a one-time operator config line, with `.nexus/worktrees/` as the default until set.
2. **Project hooks.** Run project-declared hooks after a recorded approval (recommended) versus operator-config hooks only in v1.1.3.
3. **`eval/` ownership.** WP-1302 is entirely under `eval/`, which agents are told not to touch. Name who edits it (codex-root, or explicit permission for this agent) before work starts.
4. **G1.1-4 measurement** needs the shared `GATEWAY` claim; say who schedules it.

input.command:
git mv docs/v1.1.3 docs/v1.1.4 && sed -i '24!s/1\.1\.3/1.1.4/g' docs/v1.1.4/FINDINGS.md && sed -i 's/1\.1\.3/1.1.4/g' docs/v1.1.4/PLAN.md && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/v1.1.4/PLAN.md';s=open(p).read()
i=s.index('## 6. Open decisions for the owner')
s=s[:i]+"""## 6. Owner decisions (answered 2026-11-05)
Renumbered: the v1.1.2 scope ships as v1.1.3 (the `v1.1.2` tag was rejected by the release workflow), so this plan is v1.1.4.
1. **Named worktree location:** the recommended layout. Sibling `../repo.branch` is opt-in through a one-time operator config line; `.nexus/worktrees/` stays the default until set.
2. **Project hooks:** approval-gated. Project-declared hooks run only after a recorded operator approval stored outside the repository, keyed by template hash.
3. **`eval/` (WP-1302):** codex-root edits it. This agent does not touch `eval/`.
4. **G1.1-4 measurement:** this agent (claude-code) schedules the shared `GATEWAY` claim.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git add -A docs && git commit -q -m "docs: renumber plan to v1.1.4 and record owner decisions

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -q 2>&1|tail -1
